name: Sulfacarbamide

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in Germany, first in 1988 — for liver harm and blood problems

similar.name: Sulfathiazole
problems: Pulled from the market in United States and 2 other countries, first in 1970 — for kidney harm, liver harm and serious skin reactions

similar.name: Sulfamethazine
problems: Pulled from the market in Germany, first in 1992

summary: Sulfacarbamide was pulled from the market in Germany starting in 1988 due to liver damage and blood-related harm [3]. A small computer model, not testing done on people, gave this drug a high risk score for the liver and a low risk score for the heart [M]. Similar drugs have also been removed from sales, including Sulfathiazole due to kidney, liver, and skin damage, and Sulfamethazine [4][5].
